glossary.B12: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin), from meat and fish, needed for DNA synthesis and myelin.
glossary.Vitamin B12: Cobalamin, a water-soluble vitamin from animal foods, needed for DNA synthesis and nerve myelin.
glossary.DNA synthesis: Making new DNA, needed every time a cell divides.
glossary.Anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, reducing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity.
glossary.Macrocytic anaemia: Anaemia with abnormally large red cells (MCV above 100 fL).
glossary.Water-soluble vitamin: A vitamin that dissolves in water rather than fat, such as B vitamins and vitamin C.
glossary.Autoimmune: When the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.Autoantibodies: Antibodies that wrongly target the body's own proteins or cells.
glossary.Gastric carcinoma: Stomach cancer; pernicious anaemia raises the risk through chronic atrophic gastritis.
glossary.Malabsorption: Poor absorption of nutrients from the gut, for example in coeliac or Crohn's disease.
glossary.Vegan: A diet with no animal products, so it lacks natural vitamin B12.
glossary.Alcohol excess: Drinking above safe limits; it causes poor diet and impairs folate absorption and use.
glossary.Pallor: Unusually pale skin or conjunctivae, often a sign of anaemia.
glossary.Fatigue: Persistent tiredness or lack of energy.
glossary.Hypothyroidism: An underactive thyroid gland; an autoimmune disease linked to pernicious anaemia.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: a blood test measuring haemoglobin, white cells, platelets and red cell size.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate, definitive test for a diagnosis.
glossary.Intrinsic factor antibodies: Autoantibodies against intrinsic factor; the most specific test for pernicious anaemia.
glossary.IM: Intramuscular: given by injection into a muscle.
glossary.Intramuscular: Given by injection into a muscle.
glossary.Spinal cord: The column of nerve tissue in the spine carrying messages between brain and body.
glossary.Erythroid precursors: Immature cells in the bone marrow that develop into red blood cells.
glossary.Nuclear maturation: Development of a cell's nucleus as it matures; it lags behind when DNA synthesis is slow.
glossary.Folate cycle: The chain of reactions recycling folate forms to supply building blocks for DNA.
glossary.Active folate: Tetrahydrofolate, the usable form of folate; B12 is needed to release it from methyl-folate.
glossary.Cofactor: A helper molecule an enzyme needs to work.
glossary.Neurological: Relating to the brain, spinal cord or nerves.
glossary.Masking: Folic acid corrects the blood picture in B12 deficiency, hiding it while nerve damage continues.
glossary.Bone marrow: Soft tissue inside bones where blood cells are made.
glossary.Proprioception: The sense of where your limbs are in space, carried by the dorsal columns.
